audit_scope.description: Trust model for Cancun identity precompile, EIP-7039 (SHADOW wallet discovery), EIP-2786 (Ethereum provider connection state), EIP-3091 (block explorer URLs), and Cancun stack instructions (PUSH/POP/DUP/SWAP). Covers precompile execution, wallet communication protocols, provider events, URL routing, and EVM stack operations.

out_of_scope: Provider connection events (EIP-2786 - wallet API layer)

misclassified_entities.reason: Calling Contract from Cancun identity precompile is internal to the EVM. Smart contracts invoking precompiles via CALL are within the EVM execution context, not crossing a trust boundary.
Provider State Change from EIP-2786 is an internal trigger within the provider implementation, not an external entity. It represents an internal state transition.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Provider (EIP-7039)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External wallet application responding via browser protocol handler. Could be a malicious protocol handler registration. Origin validation is critical.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blockchain Network (EIP-2786)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Underlying blockchain network the provider connects to. Network availability is not guaranteed; connection state changes trigger events to listeners.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Browser Extension (EIP-2786)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Provider object injection into web page
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Browser extension injecting Ethereum provider. Injection implies user trust but malicious extensions could inject fake providers to steal credentials.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp Client (EIP-2786)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Web application consuming the Ethereum provider API. Attaches event listeners for connection state changes.

trusted_external_entities.name: Web User (EIP-3091)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External user or application providing URL path parameters that could contain malicious input. URL path injection, XSS, and path traversal risks exist.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Wallet sends message with port. Origin must be validated before processing. First port becomes primary channel. Multiple wallets may respond.
Response must have exactly one of result or error. Origin must be verified. Invalid origins must be rejected.
Network connectivity determines provider state. Connect/disconnect events emitted to all listeners. chainId should match eth_chainId.
Injection implies user trust of the extension. Malicious extensions could inject fake providers. User must verify extension authenticity.
URL path contains untrusted resource identifiers. Must validate path format, validate identifier format (hash/address/height), prevent injection attacks.

coverage_gaps: EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT-IDENTITY and EXT-PROVIDER-STATE-CHANGE were misclassified as external
EXT-DAPP-CLIENT-2786 and EXT-BLOCKCHAIN-NETWORK-2786 edges are partially captured via related edges
Cancun stack instructions (PUSH/POP/DUP/SWAP) have no external entities - purely internal EVM operations
